title: Humpback Whales Grieve for Lost Offspring, Video Evidence Shows - Nautilus
gist: On July 17, 2025, off Australia's southern Gold Coast, a humpback whale mother stayed for hours beside her stillborn calf on the seabed, trying to keep eye contact. Video by Sea World Foundation captain Andrew Mulville is described as the first recorded grieving behavior in humpbacks.

insights.claim: On July 17, 2025, off Australia's southern Gold Coast, a humpback whale gave birth to a stillborn calf that sank to the seabed, and Sea World Foundation rescue captain Andrew Mulville filmed the event.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: An animal-cognition finding with no direct market angle.

insights.claim: The mother whale stayed near the dead calf for several hours, trying to keep eye contact and apparently looking for a response. This is reported as the first recorded grieving behavior in humpback whales.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Adds to evidence of complex emotion in cetaceans, which could strengthen arguments for marine protection policy.
insights.quote: attempting to maintain eye contact and seemingly looking for a sign of response
